nodes.label: DMA Crossover Strategy (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Single daily moving average vs. daily close, long ATM puts when below the MA. Rejected because it's strictly simpler than the existing sma.py (single MA vs. fast/slow crossover) - would add a weaker version of an existing strategy.

nodes.label: scalp Strategy
nodes.rationale: Fast BB+RSI mean-reversion on 1m candles, long+short, aimed at frequent fee-gated trades. Untuned - first backtest came back net-negative (32% win rate, -7.8%). Motivated the Position/EntryPlan side field and reduceOnly semantics.

nodes.label: sma Strategy
nodes.rationale: Trend-following crossover, kept for reference, long-only, plain market orders with no fee gate. Not the user's stated preference (trend-following has lower win rate with occasional big wins, opposite of desired risk profile).

nodes.label: Fee-vs-Edge Gate (MIN_PROFIT_TO_FEE_RATIO)
nodes.rationale: User explicitly wants fees factored into strategy decisions, not just calculated after the fact. Skips trades whose take-profit doesn't clear estimated round-trip fees by a healthy margin. Keeps a high-win-rate/small-profit strategy from being quietly eaten by costs; don't remove without checking with the user.

nodes.label: klines API Contract (POST + pair param)
nodes.rationale: /v1/market/klines is POST, not GET, and the pair parameter is named pair, not symbol - original scripts guessed GET+symbol and got 404. Response shape is a list of dicts with startTime/open/high/low/close/endTime/volume as strings.

nodes.label: JS Number Serialization Bug
nodes.community_name: Core Trading Engine & Live API Verification
nodes.rationale: Backend is almost certainly Node.js and reconstructs the signing string via JSON.stringify, which drops trailing .0 on whole-number floats (46101.0 -> "46101") while Python's json.dumps keeps it. Fixed via _js_number_safe() converting whole-number floats to int before json.dumps in signed_get/signed_post/signed_delete.

nodes.label: Signature Mismatch Bug (JSON re-serialization)
nodes.community_name: Core Trading Engine & Live API Verification
nodes.rationale: signed_post/signed_delete signed a compact JSON string but sent the request via requests.post(json=params), which requests re-serializes with different separators, so signed bytes != wire bytes. Fixed by serializing once and sending that exact string via data=data_to_sign.

nodes.label: marginAsset Always INR
nodes.rationale: Confirmed via docs.sharkexchange.in that marginAsset: "INR" is used even on non-INR pairs like BTCUSDT - the exchange is INR-margined platform-wide. shark/orders.py's hardcoded marginAsset=INR is correct as-is; don't change it to match the pair's quote currency without checking with the user.

nodes.label: limitPriceVarAllowed Constraint
nodes.rationale: exchangeInfo field capping how far a LIMIT order's price may deviate from market (0.15 i.e. 15% for BTCUSDT). Caused the test order's original 40%-below-market price to be rejected with error 3009; get_exchange_info() now surfaces it and the test script computes price as 80% of the allowed range.

nodes.label: Hedged Short Strangle Strategy (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Sells CE+PE with OTM hedge legs for defined-risk margin, SPAN-style margin sizing. Rejected outright - Shark Exchange has no options market, so there is no instrument to construct this trade with at all.

nodes.label: Leverage-Aware Position Sizing
nodes.rationale: User chose to make sizing leverage-aware rather than fund the account further or switch symbols. Two bugs caught during implementation: (1) missing INR/USDT currency conversion would have sized positions ~95x too large; (2) rounding qty down to quantityPrecision when forcing min-notional could truncate back below the minimum - fixed by rounding up in that branch specifically.

nodes.label: minNotional Small-Account Conflict
nodes.rationale: Confirmed live via /v1/exchange/exchangeInfo: per-contract order minimums (e.g. BTCUSDT 115 USDT) make a small account (~₹610) untradeable at the intended 1% risk-per-trade - clearing the minimum requires ~16-17x leverage, which would make a 1.5% stop cost ~24% of capital instead of 1%. Genuine unresolved conflict between account size and risk model, not to be silently patched.

nodes.label: walkforward_psar.py
nodes.rationale: One-off script implementing the walk-forward train/test split for psar_trend on XAUINR data; not part of the committed codebase.

nodes.label: walkforward_xauinr.py
nodes.rationale: One-off script implementing the walk-forward train/test split for mean_reversion on XAUINR data; not part of the committed codebase.

nodes.label: BTST/ORB-style Breakout Strategy (rejected)
nodes.rationale: From the user's firm's options system (BTSTDIRV2). Opening-range-breakout entry and session/DTE plumbing don't translate to crypto, but its ratcheting trailing stop/target is a more sophisticated exit mechanism than anything in this codebase - worth revisiting as an upgrade to psar_trend's exit logic later, not as a new standalone strategy.

nodes.label: mean_reversion Strategy
nodes.rationale: Chosen over trend-following per user's stated preference for consistent, lower-but-steady returns over big/volatile swings. BB+RSI+ATR, long-only, prefers maker limit orders with a fee gate. Walk-forward validated result was thin (test net +2.37% at 1h) and lost to psar_trend on every metric.

nodes.label: psar_trend Strategy
nodes.rationale: Parabolic SAR trend-following, long+short, translated from the user's firm's options trading system (only the SAR signal itself and trend-flip entry shape translate). Leading candidate as of 2026-09-16: walk-forward TEST net=+24.03%, PF=16.96, maxDD=1.03%, win 87.2%, decisively beating mean_reversion at every interval tested. Caveat: XAUINR has been in a sustained uptrend through the whole dataset, so this may reflect 'gold went up' rather than a repeatable edge; never tested against a ranging/downtrending market.

nodes.label: Walk-Forward Validation Methodology
nodes.rationale: Adopted after two false 'validated' results from tuning and validating on the same historical window (BTCUSDT 83%->66% win-rate collapse, XAUINR short-sweep mirage). Sweep on first 70% of data (train), evaluate the winning config only on the untouched last 30% (test).
